Default Current and explicit physical version selection support signing, display, verification and removal. Nested verification checks every physical version against the parent's requirement; deep checks include pages/resources/descendants. Twelve native selected-signing tree comparisons, 90 display cases, six removal comparisons, 21 shallow/deep cases and three native fixtures establish the bounded profile. Direct physical/Current version directories are supported as standalone bundles and reject additional selectors, with 64 native failure/preservation comparisons. Contents parents ignore selection and children use their own Current. Wider discovery, malformed-selector diagnostics and complete option interactions remain incomplete.

Plain Mach-O children, APPL/BNDL/XPC! Contents layouts and unversioned/multiple-version FMWK frameworks support staged descendant-first signing, preservation/force, dry-run semantics and deep page/resource/descendant verification. Signing visits only the selected version; nested verification checks every physical version against the parent's requirement. Shallow verification checks immediate child CMS/trust and non-resource metadata, including alternate versions. Layout and framework-version evidence covers native byte/display comparisons, strict deep checks, mutation cases and independent archives. Shared bounds and hard-link checks span all layouts and physical versions. Broader symlink/xattr policy, requirements/digests and full option interactions remain incomplete. Universal selection follows the arm64 baseline on every OS.

Native byte comparisons now cover 44 recorded/live standalone removal cases, eighteen complete bundle layouts and three mixed trees, without the earlier eight-byte padding exception. Symbol-table padding, LINKEDIT virtual-size preservation, universal alignment and up to seven trailing bytes match the tested native behavior. Nine re-signing cases require native byte equality and strict verification. Linux/Windows each export 44 removed outputs for native comparison. Malformed symbol ranges are rejected safely rather than reproducing native corruption. Legacy/FAT64/swapped forms, unusual layouts/unindexed padding, generic/detached representations and full diagnostic parity remain incomplete; see docs/removal.md.

Standalone Mach-O signing stages replacement through go-apfs-v2's shared metadata API, preserving other hard-link names. File aliases resolve physically before identifiers, display and writes, including link/..; alias entries remain unchanged. Bundle Mach-O writes also stage root-relative replacements; DMGs and existing resource envelopes remain in place. The 126-case bundle writer matrix checks external-link and complete-tree behavior. Fifteen hard-link cases, 150 Mach-O alias cases, ten DMG alias cases, 350 display comparisons and nine allocation-padding cases establish the bounded writer behavior alongside two-target Clang records. Re-signing preserves existing trailing allocation bytes. Darwin requires clone support and rejects protected/compressed files; wider metadata, bundle symlink and filesystem support remains incomplete. RFC 3161 verification, separate explicit TSA roots, historical certificate validity, library timestamp providers and nonce-bound SHA-256 exchanges are implemented. A public-test RSA arm64 signature exactly replays a recorded native Apple token; Apple and OpenSSL acceptance are exercised. The CLI signs with online HTTP --timestamp[=URL], verifies and displays timestamps, and supports --timestamp=none. Bundled Apple roots are explicit TSA inputs. A bounded pure-Go HTTP transport is exercised against a local authority on all targets; opt-in live Apple acceptance covers three Mach-O forms. Full TSA/Apple policy, proxy/redirect behavior, revocation, general CMS/BER and localized dates remain incomplete.

RSA/ECDSA PEM and authenticated PKCS#12 signing, native allocation, Apple BER CMS/hash agility, leaf pins and portable explicit-CA chain policy are implemented. The existing 64-case matrix is supplemented by three organization-anchor comparisons, a Developer ID csreq comparison, 24 native PKCS#12 signatures and real public Developer ID chain/Team ID checks. Authorities, fixed-format signing-time and RFC 3161 timestamp metadata are displayed. Timestamp callbacks and separate TSA trust add native replay evidence. Full PKIX/Apple policy, localized dates, end-to-end Developer ID signing, broader TSA transport policy, hybrid algorithms and revocation remain incomplete.

APPL/BNDL/XPC! Contents layouts and unversioned/multiple-version FMWK frameworks support XML/binary metadata, resources, nested code, signing, inspection, verification and outer-only removal. Explicit selection preserves other versions; nested verification applies the parent's requirement to every physical version. Direct physical/Current directories use independent resource boundaries and canonical display paths. Main-executable paths and file aliases select supported bundles by resolved filename; helpers and hard-link aliases remain standalone. Framework executable aliases select the physical version and reject further selection. Mach-O bundle writes now stage root-relative APFS replacements, preserving external hard-link neighbours; resource envelopes retain in-place/unlink semantics. The 126-case writer matrix compares complete native trees and inode effects; native executable ACL inheritance and creation-time behavior and failure-diagnostic parity remain incomplete. New signature directories copy canonical bundle-root stat metadata through APFS v0.6.0, with selected physical framework roots and unchanged existing directories. Forty directory cases and eight native security profiles cover the bounded stat profile; explicit source ACL copying and subsequent envelope inheritance remain incomplete. Regular stale signature files are purged after each rewritten main executable; removal empties only the selected signature directory and dry runs retain sidecars. A 105-case native matrix covers regular cleanup and external links. Another 210 native cases and four nested failure cases cover stale directories and internal/dangling/outside symlinks: cleanup rejects them after executable replacement, dry-run signing preserves them and succeeds, and a child failure stops the parent commit. A further 278 native comparisons cover case-insensitive APFS ASCII cleanup order, including hash collisions and entries before CodeResources. Removal rejects non-regular CodeResources after executable replacement when enumeration reaches it; signing retains early envelope rejection. PR #34 merged this ordering slice with APFS v0.6.0. This follow-up pins released v0.6.1, including APFS PR #106's public hashing API first-use race fix published through release PR #107. The dependency commit requires its own final CI/artifact validation. Bounded metadata traversal and internal write-alias rejection remain; other filesystem orders, special files, unreadable subtrees, broader permissions and raw diagnostics remain incomplete. Malformed/oversized/symlinked metadata retains stricter rejection. Relative existing resource links use symlink text seals. Staged signing constructs the complete tree before writes, with shared bounds and cross-bundle/version hard-link checks within the selected boundary. Native comparisons, mutations, Clang AST records and six fixture sets establish the bounded profile. Each Linux/Windows producer exports 45 prior app artifacts plus 63 layout archives, nine multi-version trees, nine direct-path trees, nine executable-path trees, 84 writer archives and 42 cleanup archives for native strict deep verification. Broader symlink/xattr policy, discovery, custom rules and full strict/diagnostic parity remain incomplete. See docs/bundles.md for limits.

A pinned direct go-apfs-v2/pkg/disk dependency supplies DMGFooter. Single-segment UDIF v4 signing, inspection and verification preserve payload bytes and bind the canonical trailer in slot 6. Forty ad-hoc native byte/display comparisons, fifteen ad-hoc/RSA/P-256 native signature and hdiutil checks, five native fixtures, matched-time RSA equality, local TSA tests and a live Apple timestamp establish the tested profile. Native-unsupported removal returns an error without mutation. Encrypted/segmented images, large-image streaming, detached signatures, additional digests, stapled-ticket/notarization policy and full option/diagnostic parity remain incomplete.
macOS 27 hybrid signatures and detached certificates remain incomplete.
Extended-attribute and non-Mach-O signed representations remain incomplete.
SHA-1 and alternate digest writing, scatter pages, and legacy architecture acceptance remain incomplete.
